title: Parsing Arithmetic Expressions into an AST
description: Combine the Parser monad, forward-reference cells, and a left_assoc helper to parse arithmetic expressions into Num, BinOp, and UnaryMinus AST nodes.

steps.description: Define the Parser monad class P with pure, bind, map, then, skip, alt, and many, plus the regex tokenizer helper tok(pat, fn).
Define the three AST node dataclasses: Num(value), BinOp(op, left, right), and UnaryMinus(operand).
Create FwdP forward cells for expr_p, term_p, unary_p, and primary_p, then set primary_p to match numbers or parenthesized expressions and unary_p to wrap leading '-' in UnaryMinus.
Define left_assoc(base, op_p) to fold a chain of operators left-to-right into nested BinOp(op, val, rhs) nodes, and use it to wire term_p and expr_p.

steps.question: What AST does expr_p build for '2 + 3 * 4'?
steps.answer: expr_p parses Num(2.0) via term_p, sees '+', and calls term_p on '3 * 4', which folds into BinOp('*', Num(3.0), Num(4.0)), yielding BinOp('+', Num(2.0), BinOp('*', Num(3.0), Num(4.0))).

steps.description: Write eval_ast(node) to recursively evaluate Num, UnaryMinus, and BinOp nodes, then parse and evaluate the five test strings.
